senses.gloss:
Ogaṇa is a word occurring only once, as a plural, in the Rigveda, where it appears to indicate persons hostile to the seer of the hymn, and apparently opposed to the Āryan religion. Ludwig regards the terms as the proper name of a people, but Pischel thinks that it is merely an adjective meaning ‘weak’ (ogaṇa = ava-gaṇa), as in Pāli.
Foot notes x. 89, 15
Translation of the Rigveda, 5, 209.
Vedische Studien, 2, 191, 192.
